content.text:
Operator
First question will come from the line of Neil Mehta with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.
Neil Mehta
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Good morning, Avigal team.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Morning to you. How are you?
Neil Mehta
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Good morning, sir. Couple of questions for you on the guide. The first is just capital program. To Reuven's point, Q1 of $46 million versus a full year of $330 million. Are you tracking inside of that $330 million? Is capital efficiency positively surprising, recognizing you've got the Krotz Springs turnaround? The related question to that is you've got a big turnaround across this year, later this year. How do you define success? Because I think that'll be an important test for that asset.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. First of all, thank you for the question. It's still early in the year. We are not changing our guidance. At this point, we are still with the $330 million we mentioned. In terms of the success of the KSR turnaround, I would give that three elements, right? First of all, is safety. We need to make sure that it's a safe turnaround, that everyone come back home the same way they went back to work. That's number one. Second is the scope of the work. We need to make sure that we are doing the scope right and getting the uplift of the $30 million we said before. The third, obviously, is the cost. Those are the three components.
We demonstrate to ourselves doing the Tyler turnaround, we can achieve all of those three, and we aim to achieve those in this turnaround as well.
Neil Mehta
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Thanks, Avigal. You indicated you initiated a process to unlock the value of the retail business. You know, can you talk about how it came to the decision that this makes sense to potentially monetize and where we are with the process? Are there any synergies in your early look at this process?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yes. Thanks, Neil. I will answer the question more widely about the sum of the parts efforts that we are obviously trying to do. As you probably mentioned in the call, we created the third-party value over time, and that's obviously something that is very important for us to achieve. We are committed to make sure that that value is achieved at all times. We demonstrate during this quarter that the financial strength of the DKL balance sheet is there in order to support it. That's point number two. The point number three is that we wanna make sure that the value is being created both for the DK shareholder and the DKL unit holder, and both the units show the full value.
We obviously, as we mentioned, shared that we started the formal process. The process goes as planned. I don't know, Mark, maybe you want to...
Mark Hobbs
EVP and CFO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, sure, Avigal. I'll touch on the sum of the parts initiatives as well. I just touch a few things here. You know, as Avigal mentioned earlier on the call, you know, our belief is that in order for us to highlight the hidden value that we have in the attractive midstream position that we built, in particular in the Permian Basin, we need to find the right ownership structure, you know, for those assets. I think as we've discussed clearly on prior calls, you know, we've evaluated all the options that are in front of us, the governance and tax implications of each of those.
We still wanna stress that in any action that we take ultimately on the midstream side, you know, we are focused and laser focused on ensuring that we make both Delek and Delek Logistics stronger entities from a cash flow and leverage standpoint. We don't wanna move away from that position, and that's what we're focused on. You know, on the retail front, you know, as Avigal mentioned, we have mandated an investment bank to work with us on evaluating those strategic options that are in front of us for that business. You know, things are progressing well on that front. You know, we don't have anything specific that we wanna say today, but we will come back to you know, hopefully in the near future, with some more color on that.
You know, to your point, the way that we're envisioning this is that we don't see any significant or particular dis-synergies associated with anything that we do on that front.
Neil Mehta
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Thank you, Mark.
Operator
Your next question will come from the line of Roger Read with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.
Roger Read
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Wells Fargo
Yeah, thank you. Good morning.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Morning.
Roger Read
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Wells Fargo
Maybe a little bit, I'm gonna kind of follow up on Neil's. I mean, what is the right way to think about use of funds from retail disposition or anything else? I mean, I'm thinking, you know, even wider. You've got your ownership and Wink to Webster that's held inside of DK relative to, you know, probably belongs more in a midstream sort of operation. Maybe a little more of your thoughts as you rearrange some of the pieces here to achieve that upside value for both DK and DKL. Where should we think about that working out?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, Roger, first of all, thank you for joining us today. I will start answering. Let's talk about capital allocation broader than just that. As we demonstrate in the last few quarters, we have a priority to have a consistent and growing dividend over time. We have demonstrated a few quarters now. The second priority is, we have outlined this quarter very specifically, is having a strong balance sheet, right? You probably can appreciate the major improvement that we have seen, that we have demonstrated on the DKL balance sheet. Obviously, the third point here is the buyback. I want to be clear, we see a lot of value in our share price today.
We elected not to do buybacks due to development in the strategic initiative progress. This is where we are on capital allocation. Obviously, you asked specifically about W2W. W2W always play in our toolbox that the asset develop very nicely in the last two years, and they're probably gonna receive the value of that asset going up, and it's a very premier midstream asset.
Roger Read
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Wells Fargo
Yeah, no question about that. I guess, let me pivot a little bit just to the operational front. Big Spring, been doing a lot of work there. Where are we in this process? Halfway through, three-quarters of the way through? You know, it'll take a long time to do the last 10% of improvements there, but from a reliability and an OpEx standpoint, just how that's shaping up.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, Roger. We definitely see improvement. Joseph is very close to that, so I will let him answer it.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Yes. We are executing our plans in Big Spring, and as a result, we see the improved reliability that we expected, which allows us to meet our targets, like we communicated in the past. One, run around 70,000 barrels per day on a more consistent basis. It's not Q1, but it's starting to be real here with the guidance for the Q2. Second is improve our capture toward 70%, really on mid-cycle basis. And last is to improve our cost structure. We promised a $1 per barrel per quarter reduction until we get to the mid $5 per barrel target range by the end of the year. Very happy and proud with the team and the progress that we are making.
Roger Read
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Wells Fargo
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question will come from the line of Manav Gupta with UBS. Please go ahead.
Manav Gupta
Executive Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Hey, guys. My question is more on the DKL side as it relates to DK. You know, DKL continues to be bigger and bigger part of the earnings in the last five years. As DK looks at DKL, do you see with the Permian growth, you moving in a direction where the third-party EBITDA would just continue to grow and increase versus, you know, drop-downs or organic DK contribution to DKL? I mean, just trying to understand from this point on, should we expect the DKL to continue to grow with more and more third-party EBITDA in there?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. First of all, Manav, thank you for joining us today. It's a great question. We are very proud of the progress we did. Our first priority is both unitholders and shareholders, and the value that we are creating gonna find itself into those two pockets, and that's a priority for us. Obviously, we have demonstrated first to ourselves and then to the market that we can manage those assets and can show abnormal return on them. If the opportunity presents itself, as long as it's accretive for both DK and DKL, we'll take a good hard look into that and keep developing organically and inorganically.
The answer is to the bottom line, if the opportunity presents itself, and it's a good opportunity and it can benefit both units and shares, we'll take a good hard look at that.
Manav Gupta
Executive Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Second quick question here is, look, quarter-over-quarter, three refineries showed pretty good improvement, Big Spring, Krotz Springs, and even El Dorado. I'm just trying to understand, is the kit getting to a point where you would like it to be? Obviously, there's a scope of improvement. If we look between Q4 and Q1 performance, what were some of the criteria which allowed these three assets to deliver much better earnings in Q1 versus just the last quarter?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, absolutely. Some of that is our doing, some of that is obviously the market that was better, and that's reflecting the capture rate. We obviously gave a clear guidance to the OpEx that shows better even in Q2 versus Q1. Joseph, why don't you chime in and give some more color into that?
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. So far it has been mainly playing defense, right? In Q1, if you count the $3.50 per barrel LPO in Big Spring and the $1.50 per barrel headwind on the OpEx, this is $30 million that was left on the table related to the freeze events, right? To answer your question, as we have lost less and less surprises and headwind to deal with, we are more and more focused on transitioning to offense and optimize our business, thinking more about process optimization, selecting the right crude, making the right product, taking it to the right markets. At the end of the day, it will translate to a much better capture, and the market will get a chance to see the true profitability option of this system.
Manav Gupta
Executive Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Thanks, guys, and congrats on a stronger quarter, and keep up the good work. Thank you.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Thank you.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you, Manav. Thank you again.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Paul Cheng with Scotiabank. Please go ahead.
Paul Cheng
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Scotiabank
Hi. Good morning, guys.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Morning, Paul.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Good morning, Paul.
Paul Cheng
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Scotiabank
Joseph, just curious. I mean, you get hit, as you mentioned earlier, that on this winter storm, Big Spring, you estimate that it's close to $5 impact, both in the profit margin as well as on the cost. Krotz Springs is another, say, 21.50 odd, right? Maybe I got it wrong, but also that have maybe at least $1.50 on the impact. What's the lesson that we learned from that? Is that something that you can do to prevent it? Because the winter storm is actually well telegraphed way beforehand. Is there anything operationally that we can do in order to minimize that kind of impact? That's the first question.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Yes. Thank you for the question. First, I will correct one thing. The $1.50 per barrel in Krotz Springs was related to a planned catalyst cleaning in the coker unit, so we knew about it coming into the quarter. It has been a long cycle and to make it all the way to the turnaround and get you the maximum throughput through the driving season, we executed the scope in a low margin environment, and I'm very glad we did it. In Big Spring, it was really the typical challenges of freeze, right? I mean, frozen lines, instrumentation like our peers dealt with. What are we doing? What are the lessons? It's all about risk mitigation.
You think about people, process, equipment, and our main job here is to mitigate the risk each and every day and to better position the asset to deal with every possible challenge and whatever the market gives to us. Very proud of the team. Looking at Q2, we are ready to run, and I think good things are coming our way.
Paul Cheng
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Scotiabank
Second question. On the supply and marketing, you said that wholesale lost $60 million in the quarter. I think in the past, you sort of giving a kind of guidance saying that the wholesale will be doing roughly about $30 million a quarter, and our spot will be lower in Q1 and Q4, maybe at $5 million, and then in Q2 and Q3 will be somewhere in the $15 million. For a full year, about $40 million. Based on what we've seen in the last several quarters, is those guidance still a good one or that internally that you guys have built them somewhat differently?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. I will start, Paul, with your permission, and then I will allow Joseph to give some more colors around that question. Great question. First of all, we need to start that wholesale is a strategic key part of a downstream integrated business unit. We see the value in that. We see our ability to place products in a different market conditions. We need to remember that when we are looking in wholesale, right? That's the first part. The second part, it's a bit more tricky to model wholesale because of the dynamic nature of that business. That business is changing every day, and the market are very dynamic. It's a bit. It's not as simple to model it, and that's the reason we are not giving always clear guidance about that.
I know that Joseph put a lot of thinking into that topic, so please.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, Paul, first, to answer your question, I think the real answer is no. I mean, that range is probably not a good place to be. When you look at the full year 2023, supply and marketing still made +$50 million, right? So statistically, we averaged slightly over $10 million positive contribution per quarter. However, it's a very hard number to model. Like Avigal said, it's very important to realize we are an integrated downstream company, and the wholesale marketing is playing a strategic role to connect between our refineries to the customers. We move around 210,000 barrels per day of products through that wholesale marketing, which is approximately 800 million gallons per quarter.
High level, it takes a -7.5 cents per gallon margin between the pricing differential and RINs to get to a $60 million loss type of number. I'm sure you and others who follow the screen remember the -30, 35 cents per gallon back in January through the Midcon freeze. I think our team is doing great job in mitigating this risk going forward, diversifying our pricing exposure and footprint, and hopefully we're gonna do better in these type of situations in the future.
Paul Cheng
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Scotiabank
All right. Will do. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question will come from the line.[crosstalk]
Your next question will come from the line of John Royall with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.
John Royall
VP and Equity Research Analyst, JPMorgan
Hi. Good morning. Thanks for taking my question. So I just had a follow-up on capital allocation. I guess it's a two-parter. One is, you've hiked your dividend now. I think seven quarters in a row, up 25% over that time period. Should we expect that to continue with the more frequent but smaller hikes, or will you get to the point where you move to more of a once-a-year type cadence? Then, the second part is just on the buyback, which you talked about the reasoning for turning it off in Q1. What's a reasonable expectation for when you might be back in the market for buybacks?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. I will answer both of those questions more broadly, and I will not be as specific. As I said all along, being a shareholder-friendly company is a key priority for us, as long as maintaining a strong balance sheet. We definitely will maintain that. As I said, a few times, having a consistent and growing dividend over time is something that we value, and we believe our investors value as well. Both of them are very key priorities for us. Around the buyback, I want to make a point very clear. We've seen a lot of value in our share price, but we elected not to do it, because of developments in the strategic initiative and the progress we have made around it.
John Royall
VP and Equity Research Analyst, JPMorgan
Great. Thank you. Can you talk about the timing of separating retail? I realize these processes don't just kick off overnight, but it's a little bit of a tougher time fundamentally now, at least over the short term, on fuel margin and also on merchandise sales. Do you think the enthusiasm for this business and the asset sale market is maybe what it was six or 12 months ago? Or do you think buyer expectations have adjusted at all?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, we obviously are not gonna be specific around the process. We have a great asset, a unique market position, a unique market. We are making good progress.
John Royall
VP and Equity Research Analyst, JPMorgan
Okay. Thank you.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yes. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question will come from the line of Ryan Todd with Piper Sandler. Please go ahead.
Ryan Todd
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
Thank you. Maybe if we think about your refining EBITDA over the last four quarters, I think you've generated around $580 million of EBITDA in an environment that was generally above historical mid-cycle margins. As you think about your refining business going forward, what do you believe is the mid-cycle EBITDA or earnings power of the business as currently constituted? And how do you maybe think about the bridge of where it is versus where you want it to be, whether in terms of cost reductions, reliability improvements, ability to repatriate EBITDA out of DKL back into DK? Like, how do you want the market to think about, how should we be thinking about the mid-cycle earnings power of your refining business?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Ryan, thank you for the great question. As we said in the past, we believe that our earning power in refining is improving as we speak. We have seen better capture rates. You have seen that in all refineries, and we have seen that we demonstrate lower and lower LPO. That's a key part of that. Joseph put a lot of time into that, so maybe, Joseph, you want to take this one?
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. We think on a mid-cycle basis, our mid-cycle EBITDA is between $750 to $800 million.
Ryan Todd
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
At the refining level?
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US Holdings
No, this is for the entire company, and this is considering a stable refining segment with minimum surprises as we position it.
Ryan Todd
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
Okay. Perfect. Thank you. Maybe I guess it probably feeds into that some, but I don't know if I missed it earlier or not. Can you update us as to, like, progress to date on the cost reduction target? I know you talked about the $90 to $100 million, you know, kind of run rate for 2024. Are you there? Where have you seen the greatest improvement so far? What's worked well? What still remains to be done? Maybe just an update in terms of the process there.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Absolutely. We are focusing to be at around $90 to $100 billion exiting 2024. We have found additional opportunities in towards 2025, and that goes very well. Reuven and his team is doing an amazing job around it. Reuven, you wanna add anything?
Reuven Spiegel
EVP of Special Projects, Delek US Holdings
Well, we have executed most of the steps that we planned thus far. We have two more steps in Q2 and Q3 that will put us on track for $90 to $100 million. We have identified opportunities between $15 to $20 million that will be executed in 2025.
Ryan Todd
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Piper Sandler
Great. Thank you.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question will come from the line of Matthew Blair with TPH. Please go ahead.
Matthew Blair
Managing Director and Lead Equity Research Analyst, TPH
Thank you and good morning. There's some reports that Wink-to-Webster will be offline in January for up to two weeks. Is that correct? And what kind of market impact would you anticipate? And if that did widen out Midland spreads, do you think Delek would be in a position to benefit there?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. Matthew, thank you for the question. Obviously, I'm not gonna comment about W-to-W operation. We are not the operator of the line, and we are not commenting on those kind of rumors or news. Regarding the spread, I think that everyone can see that the Longhorn spread, i.e. Midland MEH, is widening pretty nicely. We see it in June widening all the way to $2.00 in H2. Q4, I think it's like $0.75 now. That's a demonstration of increase in production. We see the production in Midland 6.5, 6.6 million barrels per day, and probably gonna go up this year on the additional 250 to 300 thousand barrels a day.
That's put the Midland differentials going into the next half, which is the Basin and the Cushing. That's gonna widen the differential just a little bit. That's obviously a very good development for us.
Matthew Blair
Managing Director and Lead Equity Research Analyst, TPH
Sounds good. Circling back to the commentary on supply and marketing,
You mentioned you're seeing some seasonal demand improvement. You're rolling off the very negative values in January, but we also see RINs, you know, 10% to 15% lower. Putting that all together, do you think supply and marketing can be positive EBITDA contribution in Q2 after the $65 million loss in Q1?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah, Matthew. It's still early in the quarter. We believe in the business, but I'm not gonna give guidance for that. We gave a lot of guidance that help you to model really well. It's really hard to predict the dynamic in the market at this second, so I'm gonna stay out of that guidance.
Matthew Blair
Managing Director and Lead Equity Research Analyst, TPH
Okay. Sounds good. Thanks.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question will come from the line of Jason Gabelman with TD Cowen. Please go ahead.
Jason Gabelman
Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, TD Cowen
Yeah. Hey, morning. Thanks for taking my questions. I wanted to go back to the marketing business and just how you're evaluating unlocking value there. I think when you started this value unlock process a little over a year ago, marketing was considered a core part of the business and wasn't something you were gonna look to really try to monetize, and it sounds like that's changed. Just wondering over the past year why that's changed.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. Jason, thank you for the question. Obviously, our commitment, as I said many times, is to make sure that our investors see the value in both the unit price and the share price here. We are taking a good, hard look at everything, and that's something we decided that we need to look at the opportunities. I think that's what a prudent management needs to do, and that's what we are doing.
Jason Gabelman
Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, TD Cowen
Okay, thanks. Yeah. Just, I guess, on the supply and trading line, as we think about it moving forward, and I know you wanna stay away from really providing concrete guidance, but I'm just wondering if you see any headwinds when your assets aren't operating at 100% and you try to buy product in the market to fulfill contractual obligations. Was that an impact in Q1, and is that something we could think about maybe not recurring moving forward?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. I don't want to get into too much into the weeds here. Obviously, having a safe and reliable operation has a very broad benefits. There is a reason, Jason, that I'm very determined about the safe and reliable operation. That's actually priority. Without getting too much technicalities about how each one of the entity works with the other, I will just tell you that this is a commitment, and that's a priority, and we are driving a lot of energy into that, and I will leave it to that.
Jason Gabelman
Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, TD Cowen
All right. Thanks for the answers.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Thank you.
Operator
There are no further questions at this time. I will now hand the call back to Avigal for any closing remarks.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US Holdings
Yeah. Thank you. So I want to thank our employees for their hard commitment for the success of this company. I want to thank you, shareholders, for trusting in us and the interest that you are showing around our business. I want to thank our loyal customers, and I want to thank our board of directors for their support, good advice, and commitment. Obviously, I want to thank my colleagues here around the table that's working days and nights in order to make this company what it is. Thank you, guys.
Operator
That will conclude today's conference. Thank you all for joining. You may now disconnect.

content.text:
Operator
Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the Delek US Q4 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all lines are in listen-only mode. Following the presentation, we will conduct a question and answer session. If at any time during this call you require immediate assistance, please press star zero for the operator. This call is being recorded on Tuesday, 27 February 2024. I would now like to turn the conference over to Rosy Zuklic, VP Investor Relations. Please go ahead.
Rosy Zuklic
VP of Investor Relations, Delek US
Good morning and welcome to the Delek US Q4 Earnings Conference Call. Participants on today's call will include Avigal Soreq, President and CEO, Joseph Israel, EVP Operations, Reuven Spiegel, EVP and Chief Financial Officer, and Mark Hobbs, EVP Corporate Development. Today's presentation material can be found on the investor relations section of the Delek US website. Slide two contains our safe harbor statement regarding forward-looking statements. We'll be making forward-looking statements during today's call. These statements involve risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ materially from today's comments. Factors that could cause actual results to differ are included here as well as in our SEC filings. The company assumes no obligation to update any forward-looking statements. I will now turn the call over to Avigal for opening remarks.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Thank you, Rosy. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today. During Q4, our operation ran well at the higher end of our guidance. We did a good job of focusing on what we could control. With that, I would like to thank each member of the Delek team. From a market perspective, during the quarter, we saw a weakness in product demand consistent with the seasonal trend. In Refining, we achieved a record total throughput in the quarter, but still see opportunities for further operational improvements. Joseph will provide the details of our refinery operation and progress at Big Spring. We delivered another record quarter in our Logistics segment. The consistent strong performance from our Logistics segment validates our favorable position in the Permian Basin. Our Israel segment reported its best Q4 outside of COVID year 2020.
Turning to the full year, 2023 was a strong year for Delek. We achieved $950 million of adjusted EBITDA. We made significant progress on our key objectives. As a reminder, they are operational excellence, financial strength, shareholder return, and executing our strategic initiatives. In terms of operational excellence, our team delivered a solid performance across all businesses this year. We made strategic investment in our people and assets. This improved our foundation for profitable and sustainable growth. Our planned major turnaround of the Tyler Refinery was completed on time, on budget, and with no recordable incidents. The result was improved reliability, yield recovery, and stronger capturing. We are very focused on our safety practices and pushing for constant improvement. I am pleased to report that 2023 was our best year on record for safety performance. This includes personal and process safety.
Turning to financial strength and shareholder returns, we continue to be shareholder-friendly. In 2023, we returned $146 million to shareholders through dividend and share buyback. We also improved our financial position by using our strong cash flow to reduce debt by $454 million. We made progress on our strategic initiatives. As a result of our cost reduction efforts, we found more efficient ways of working. This has delivered tangible results. For example, our inventory management has resulted in improvement in both earnings and debt levels. We are making progress to reach our goal of $100 million run rate cost reduction. Lastly, significant headway was made towards unlocking intrinsic value in our business. Now, turning to 2024. Our key priorities have not wavered. We'll continue our drive towards operational excellence, staying focused on safe and reliable operations.
We have turnaround of our Krotz Springs Refinery in Q4 of 2024. Joseph will give context on the improvement we expect post-turnaround. We'll also talk about additional initiatives we are undertaking in the Refining segment. Financial strength and shareholder return will remain key. We believe we are well-positioned to capture opportunities. We'll continue our disciplined capital allocation with the best interest of our stakeholder in mind. We look to deliver strong portfolio performance and results. We'll continue to optimize the balance sheet and remain committed to sustainable and competitive shareholder returns. In 2023, we returned $146 million to shareholders. $85 million of this was share buyback. As we demonstrate in 2023, we are committed to shareholder returns based upon free cash flow.
As we execute 2024, we'll remain and maintain this approach, and we'll keep balanced approach between improving our financial strength and shareholder returns. On our strategic initiatives, we'll remain focused in advance. For 2024, we estimate our CapEx to be approximately $330 million, which reflects a reduction from 2023 levels. The capital program shows our dedication to maintain and safe reliable operation, enhancing our portfolio with strategic growth projects, and delivering shareholder value while maintaining our financial strength and flexibility. In 2024, we will continue to explore opportunities in the energy transition space that meet our return to capital objectives.
We announced earlier this month that our Big Spring Refinery was selected by the Department of Energy for a project that will advance carbon capture technology in a safe, environmentally responsible manner. This project will serve our industry well into the decades to come. Now, I would like to turn the call over to Joseph, who will provide additional details on our operations.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US
Thank you, Avigal. Moving to slide five through seven. In Q4, our team processed a back-to-back record high 306,000 barrels per day of total throughput. In Tyler, total throughput in Q4 was approximately 79,000 barrels per day. Production margin in the quarter was $11.54 per barrel, and operating expenses were $5.13 per barrel, which reflects approximately $0.55 per barrel of an employee benefit accrual and accelerated tank farm work. In Q1, the estimated total throughput in Tyler is in the 71,000 to 74,000 barrels per day range. In El Dorado, total throughput in the quarter was approximately 88,000 barrels per day, a record-high throughput for the plant.
Our production margin was $4.94 per barrel, and operating expenses were $4.58 per barrel. Estimated throughput for Q1 is in the 82,000 to 85,000 barrels per day range. After working the El Dorado fundamentals in the past several years and improving reliability, the team is focused on profit improvement opportunities, mainly in the crude sourcing, asphalt, and wholesale areas. By accessing heavier grades in El Dorado, we will use existing refinery configuration to improve asphalt capabilities and optimize margins. By increasing regional sales of our pipeline on the light product side, we will improve commercial optionality. In Big Spring, total throughput for the quarter was approximately 58,000 barrels per day, driven by maintenance work, mostly reflected in our guidance, but with additional discoveries that we've addressed.
Our production margin was $6.05 per barrel, including an estimated unfavorable $3.40 per barrel impact from the maintenance activities. Operating expenses in Big Spring were $8.98 per barrel, including approximately $1.90 per barrel related to the additional maintenance, $1.40 per barrel for the integrity program, and $0.40 per barrel related to employee benefit accrual. Estimated throughput for Q1 is in the 63,000 to 66,000 barrels per day range. In Krotz Springs, total throughput was approximately 81,000 barrels per day. Our production margin was $4.93 per barrel, and operating expenses were $4.83 per barrel.
The Krotz Springs team is preparing for the Q4 turnaround, which will include regular maintenance as well as major upgrades to our FCC and crude units. Execution cost is estimated at $115 million, and expected return from the upgrades is approximately $30 million per year, coming mainly from yield and rate flexibility improvement and energy efficiency. Plant throughput for Q1 is in the 73,000 to 76,000 barrels per day range. For our entire refining system, implied throughput target is in the 289,000 to 301,000 barrels per day range as we position ourselves for the gasoline season. In Q4, wholesale marketing contributed a loss of approximately $20 million.
This is a $40 million negative variance to the Q3. The decrease reflects seasonal trends, along with challenging mid-con supply demand dynamics and lower RINs prices. We are expecting our commercial initiatives to provide us with better optionality in the future. Asset marketing contributed approximately $5 million, compared with $50 million in the Q3, and consistent with our seasonal trends. In summary, 2023 was an important and successful year for our system in many ways. Our focus on people, process, and equipment is giving us a strong foundation to optimize what we have and position our system for growth.
While Tyler, Krotz Springs, and El Dorado have optimized operations over the years, we remain confident about our progress in Big Spring's reliability ahead of the coming gasoline season. US refining market dynamics for 2024 are constructive, and we are well-positioned to capture these opportunities. I will now turn the call over to Rosy for the financial variance.
Rosy Zuklic
VP of Investor Relations, Delek US
Thanks, Joseph. Starting on slide eight. For Q4 2023, Delek US had a loss of $165 million or $2.57 per share. Adjusted net loss was $93 million or $1.46 per share, and adjusted EBITDA was $61 million. Cash flow from operations was $91 million. On slide nine, the waterfall of adjusted EBITDA from Q3 to Q4 2023 shows that the primary driver for the lower results was from Refining. This reflects the significantly lower cracks in Q4 relative to Q3. Logistics set a new record quarter at over $99 million. Retail was down largely due to seasonal trends. Although we were in a falling crude environment, we saw lower margins but maintained strong volumes at our stores.
Corporate segment costs improved compared with last quarter, largely due to lower employee benefit expenses. Moving on to slide 10 to discuss the cash flow. We drew $80 million in cash during the quarter, ending Q4 with a balance of $822 million. Cash flow from operations, as I said, was $91 million. Included in this amount is +$223 million of working capital. This was largely from improved inventory management and lower product prices reflected in receivables. Investing activities of $69 million is mainly for capital expenditures. Financing activities of $101 million primarily reflects pay-down of debt and return to shareholders. This includes $41 million debt repayment, $20 million in buybacks, $15 million in dividends, and $10 million in distribution payments.
On slide 11, we have the breakout of the 2023 capital program and guidance for 2024. Full year 2023 was $372 million. Approximately 80% of the spend was for sustaining and regulatory projects, which include the major turnaround at the Tyler Refinery and reliability work at the Big Spring Refinery. Our forecasted 2024 capital program is $330 million, which include $255 million for sustaining and regulatory projects and $75 million for growth projects. In Refining, we plan to invest $220 million, with 93% of the capital dedicated towards sustaining and regulatory projects, most of which is for the Krotz Springs Refinery major turnaround scheduled during Q4 2024, as well as projects at the Big Spring Refinery to improve capture rates.
In Logistics, the company expects the capital program to be approximately $70 million, with $50 million for growth projects. Growth projects will advance new connections in both the Midland and Delaware gathering systems, enabling continued volume growth at the partnership. The Retail segment capital expenditures are expected to be approximately $15 million. Funds are dedicated to maintaining Delek's 250 convenience stores, including interior rebranding and re-imaging initiatives. The corporate and other segment includes approximately $25 million of capital expenditures, which is primarily to fund IT improvements. Net debt is broken out between Delek and Delek Logistics on slide 12.
During the quarter, we drew $80 million of cash and paid down $41 million of debt, ending the quarter with a net debt position of $78 million. Finally, slide 13 covers outlook items. In addition to the guidance Joseph provided, for Q1 2024, we expect operating expenses to be between $215 and 225 million, G&A to be between $60 and 65 million, D&A to be between $90 and 95 million, and net interest expense to be between $80 and 85 million. We will now open the line for questions.
Operator
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question-and-answer session. Should you have a question, please press star followed by the one on your touch-tone phone. You will hear a three-tone prompt that your hand has been raised. Should you wish to decline from the polling process, please press star followed by the two. If you are using a speakerphone, please lift the handset before pressing any keys. One moment please for your first question. Your first question comes from Neil Mehta with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.
Neil Mehta
Head of Americas Natural Resources Equity Research, Goldman Sachs
Yeah. Thank you so much, team. I guess the first question is just an update on the sum of the parts unlock. I know, Avigal, it's something you've talked about over the last couple of years, and your latest thinking around that and the milestones we should be watching on that.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Hey, Neil. How are you? Yeah, Neil, you know how much energy we have around the topic and, the way they're doing the content, significant headway, and, some of the parts going to happen. I want to assure you that. Mark, you want to add, more?
Mark Hobbs
EVP of Corporate Development, Delek US
Yeah, Neil. Look, at this point, I would say, look, although we don't have anything specific to update or say at this time, but we remain committed to highlighting the value that's intrinsic in our business. Look, we're working hard towards that. What I would say that in anything that we may do, we are very focused on enhancing, not only our balance sheet across all of our businesses, but positioning our company to generate and deliver, you know, attractive shareholder returns for the foreseeable future. We're taking all of those things into consideration.
Neil Mehta
Head of Americas Natural Resources Equity Research, Goldman Sachs
Okay.
Mark Hobbs
EVP of Corporate Development, Delek US
I'll just sort of leave it at that for now.
Neil Mehta
Head of Americas Natural Resources Equity Research, Goldman Sachs
Yeah.
Mark Hobbs
EVP of Corporate Development, Delek US
I appreciate it.
Neil Mehta
Head of Americas Natural Resources Equity Research, Goldman Sachs
Yeah. We'll stay tuned.
Mark Hobbs
EVP of Corporate Development, Delek US
Yeah.
Neil Mehta
Head of Americas Natural Resources Equity Research, Goldman Sachs
The follow-up is just on the quarter, was a little bit softer than what we expected. I guess I'd love your perspective on maybe some one-time impact. Sounds like marketing could be a dynamic there. As we think about the sequential build from Q4 to Q1, as mid-con margins have strengthened a little bit through the quarter, do you have anything that you would want us to keep in mind as we think about incrementals and decrementals?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Yes. Yeah. Sure, Neil. You can see it. Very easy to see that we had a record throughput during the quarter, and we actually meet all the guidance to give in terms of G&A, OpEx, very strong cash flow. Supply and Marketing obviously had a weaker, which is in line with seasonal trend. We've seen the line of Supply and Marketing flat in the previous quarter and a big positive in Q2. There is some seasonality into that line, which is more market driven. Listen, we are focusing on what we can control, and we did a good job during the quarter. Joseph, I don't know if you have anything to add into that.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US
Yeah. The wholesale marketing contributed -$20 million, asphalt deposit of $5 million, consistent with the seasonal trends. Wholesale marketing was challenged, and I think you heard it from most refiners beyond seasonal trends driven by inclement weather in the mid-con. The weather kept the demand and margins low, especially in December and going through the January freeze. The other element in Q4 was the lower RIN price, which has helped the refining capture but hurt the range value really generated by wholesale marketing, you know, the blended at this point. In the past several weeks, to your point, Neil, the high inventory situation in the mid-con has resolved through both supply and demand fronts. The commercial optionality focus in El Dorado, which we discussed in the preceding months, will help us in the future to navigate through this type of, say, volatility.
Neil Mehta
Head of Americas Natural Resources Equity Research, Goldman Sachs
Okay. Thanks, Joseph. Thanks, team.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US
Thank you.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from John Royall with J.P. Morgan. Please go ahead.
John Royall
Executive Director, J.P. Morgan
Hi. Good morning. Thanks for taking my question. My first one's on working capital. You've talked about the inventory management side, and you mentioned there wouldn't be a reversal of Q3's tailwind. It looks like not only did it not reverse, but you had an even bigger tailwind in Q4, despite the falling crude price. Can you speak a little bit more to your efforts around working capital and inventory management? And is there more to go there? Should we expect further working capital tailwinds going forward, all other things equal?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Yeah, absolutely, John. I would ask Reuven maybe to give you some more color around it.
Reuven Spiegel
EVP and CFO, Delek US
Sure. Good morning, and thank you for the question. I mean, we took a more holistic view around our balance sheet health from the beginning of the year. Q3 and Q4 working capital were really the fruition of some of the initiatives that we had all along. Obviously, managing and optimizing inventory was one of them. We did a big chunk of it in Q3, but we completed the work in Q4, and that contributed roughly $190 million to working capital. In addition to that, we had the ZBB effort, which we already accomplished on a run rate $80 million saving a year, of which $57 million were realized in 2023, mostly in Q3 and Q4.
Our focus was debt reduction, so we reduced by roughly $450 million. That, along with the safety and reliability efforts, kind of contributed to the end result of the working capital. I think, with regard to going forward, we kind of reached an equilibrium at the level of inventory we wanna manage. It will be more a result of you know quarterly events that will impact the working capital in the future.
John Royall
Executive Director, J.P. Morgan
Great. That's really helpful detail. Thank you. Then, can you talk about some of the opportunities you mentioned around energy transition? I think you mentioned carbon capture at Big Spring. Is this committed at this point, and is there any capital in the 2024 budget for this? Can you also remind us just on the status of the option you've had on the renewable side that you've spoken to in the past?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Yeah, absolutely, John. At this point, we were elected to negotiate with the DOE, so there is no material capital for 2024, and we're gonna do everything we're gonna do under the strict benchmark that we put on ourselves from a cost of capital return or from IRR standpoint. We're not gonna break that metric. John, from a holistic standpoint, you can see a very nice testament that Big Spring and Delek are a market leader in this area, and we're elected the first refinery to elect to be elected as energy transition by the DOE, which is a very big deal. We believe that those projects will be further in the future, and we will make it a capital advantage or capital to meet our capital benchmark.
Around the option we have on the renewable diesel, we are looking at that carefully. Obviously, it's a cheap way to get a look into renewable diesel. As you can see, RINs prices don't have renewable diesel lately, so we are fortunate not to commit $200 to 300 million and then not benefit from that. We were fortunate around it, but the market is very close to that. I don't know, Mark, if you wanna add anything around the option.
Mark Hobbs
EVP of Corporate Development, Delek US
Yeah, sure. Around the option, John, we're obviously monitoring it very closely. Our understanding based on publicly available information is that they're intending to start commission the facility in Q1, and then we will watch it as it runs through Q1 and Q2. Once they hit a run rate for, you know, 90 days at 80% utilization, then that's when we would have the opportunity to take a look at it. But, you know, we're monitoring it closely. As Avigal said, it's a. It could be potentially an attractive and low cost opportunity for us to acquire a meaningful, position in a well located renewable diesel facility. We're watching it closely.
John Royall
Executive Director, J.P. Morgan
Thank you.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Thank you, John. Appreciate it.
Operator
Your next question comes from Roger Read with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.
Roger Read
Senior Energy Analyst, Wells Fargo
Yeah, thank you. Good morning.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Morning.
Roger Read
Senior Energy Analyst, Wells Fargo
Just two questions for me, both on the operational side. Just again, to follow up on the supply and marketing sort of, let's call it headwinds in Q4. Is there anything as you look at Q1 that says that does reverse, right? I mean, I know it's market conditions. There's a limit to what you can, let's say, you know, the buttons you can push to change that, but maybe just give us an idea of how that's kind of evolved, the first couple months of this year.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Yeah. We are not gonna give the guidance for that line. It's gonna be sort of fit with the market, what the market usually gives, so we'll be consistent with our peers around it. Overall, there is a positive trend correlated to seasonal, driving seasonal. We all seen the information around the, from a macro standpoint, around gasoline and diesel. Gasoline, we are looking at around the five-year average, a bit below. On diesel, we are at the lower end of the five-year average. Both look constructive. Beyond the general market information, we are not gonna give a guidance for supply and marketing.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US
Yeah, nothing to add.
Rosy Zuklic
VP of Investor Relations, Delek US
Can I just add one thing? I think the only thing I would maybe add, Roger, is the fact that some of the weather impacts that Joseph referred to, and he said it in his prepared remarks, were persistent through January. You know, I think others saw that. That would be the one thing that I would just be mindful of, that that obviously it will be reflected in that line.
Roger Read
Senior Energy Analyst, Wells Fargo
Okay, fair enough. Although, I guess it seems the weather's more benign here as we are 2/3 of the way through, so maybe you'll get a tailwind. The other question I have, and this is on slide seven, Big Spring Refinery has been, you know, typically we think of it as one of the better units overall in the company, but it's been, you know, challenged here recently. You've got the reliability improvement, the $100 million, you know, 2/3 roughly this year, a third next year. What would you point to as we look at, you know, let's call it progress Q1 and Q2 of the year, that are gonna get capture rate above 70? I mean, is it just that the unit should run more consistently?
Is there some actual changes in the facilities that would affect yield, a change in crews you're gonna put in there, something along those lines? Maybe just kinda help us understand what we should look for as the favorable road signs as we go through 2024.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Yeah, for sure. Joseph will give a complete answer, but I will say just as from a big picture standpoint, Big Spring is a refinery that's been used to run consistent 70,000 barrels a day of throughput and more, and with a $5.25 OpEx and less. You can see that was the trend years before. There is no reason we cannot bring it back to where it used to be. That's the highlight of the $100 million. If we run it consistently as that refinery used to run in the past, there is no reason we cannot get to what it used to run years ago. Joseph, please.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US
Yeah. As we mentioned in the preliminary remarks, we are positioning Big Spring availability to serve us well already through the coming gasoline season. We've been on clear execution path, addressing the people, process, equipment gaps. As we mitigate the different risks, we should see improved reliability, meaning lower slop oil, better capture, lower cost structure. As we communicated in the past, we are expecting the throughput to stabilize north of 70,000 and capture around 17%. We are killing it, Roger, on mid-cycle basis. OpEx run rate should stabilize around $5.60, probably, per barrel by end of the year, and a linear reduction, maybe we'll say $1 per barrel reduction every quarter until end of the year would probably be a good assumptions.
Bottom line is, it will take all of the above, people, process, equipment to get to where we wanna get. We are really encouraged by the process. We have less and less surprises as the time goes by, and we are really confident about our capabilities already this coming year, spring.
Roger Read
Senior Energy Analyst, Wells Fargo
All right. Appreciate that. Thanks.
Operator
Your next question comes from Matthew Blair with TPH. Please go ahead.
Matthew Blair
Managing Director, TPH
Thank you and good morning. I wanted to follow up on some of the past efforts and appreciate your hard work here. My question is, could you talk about your openness to a sale of your retail assets? How attractive would a retail sale be relative to some other options that you might have?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Yeah. Matthew, that's a great question. Everything is on the table, and we are active more than one front line, so absolutely.
Matthew Blair
Managing Director, TPH
Okay.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Please go on.
Matthew Blair
Managing Director, TPH
Okay. Then my follow-up is on your trading and supply activities. What do you think normalized annual EBITDA for this line item should be? I have an old note in here that says roughly $130 to 210 million as an annual ballpark figure, and I think that compares to roughly $50 million in 2023. What do you think, you know, going forward, trading and supply should contribute on an annual basis?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Matthew, we don't give guidance for that line. We will remain consistent with that, with the best practice among our peers. Rosy, I think you have a lot of energy around that topic, so.
Rosy Zuklic
VP of Investor Relations, Delek US
Yeah. You know, the thing I would say is you may have an old note based on what previously we would have in there, and as you said, trading and supply. The line is no longer trading and supply. It's supply and marketing. Again, what we have in there is three components. There's the wholesale marketing, there's the asphalt marketing, and then we have the supply business. You know, the wholesale marketing and the asphalt business, tend to have a little bit more stability. Now, they do have fluctuations based on market conditions.
You know, case in point, what Joseph spoke about the fact that, you know, we had a $40 million variance between Q3 and Q4 because of the mid-con environment that we saw in Q4 relative to Q3, and then obviously the movement in the RIN prices. Asphalt tends to be a little bit more stable. You've got seasonality with the fact that the quarters during the summer months tend to be more stable and stronger. You've got Q1 and Q4 being a little bit on the weaker side. I think Q4 is a good indicator of what a Q1, Q4 tend to look like. You've got stronger quarters in the middle.
The third component being the supply, that one's the one that's a little bit harder to model because you know, the supply business handles both supplying our refineries from a crude perspective and also unloading the refineries and also supplying our DKL system, right? And so depending on disruptions throughout the entire system, you may have a little bit of fluctuation, right? But the other two pieces are a little bit easier to model.
Matthew Blair
Managing Director, TPH
Great. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from Kalei Akamine with Bank of America. Please go ahead.
Kalei Akamine
Research Analyst, Bank of America
Hey, guys. Doug sends his regards from the West Coast. I've just got a couple also on slide number six here. I guess the first question is on the Krotz turnaround. Just hoping that you can give us some idea of the scope of the work that you're performing and how that could potentially drive better commercial performance on the back end, whether that's reliability or whether that's in yield. I guess same question for El Dorado as you're thinking about the commercial opportunities there.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Yeah. Joseph will start with the answer about the Krotz Springs, and I will give some more color around the El Dorado.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US
Yes. First, I'd like to remind everyone that we guided an annualized $18 million improvement ahead of the final turnaround, which we achieved on apples to apples and market condition assumptions. We actually achieved $24 million, but the margins were better, so it's exactly what we expected. Now back to Krotz. We are expecting $30 million run rate coming from maybe three things. One is a crude unit piping scope that will help our yield and rate flexibility. In other words, we will make more jet fuel and have more cat capacity. Second is FCCU. We're gonna put a new reactor in there. We will make some regenerator upgrades that will provide us with improved conversion and yields. In addition, we are expecting better energy efficiency with a couple of turbines that we are replacing and higher reformer catalyst activity post turnaround.
Kalei Akamine
Research Analyst, Bank of America
I appreciate that.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US
Thank you.
Kalei Akamine
Research Analyst, Bank of America
Go ahead.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
If you want some highlights around El Dorado, Joseph prepared in his prepared remarks that we are planning to run a bit more heavy slate in El Dorado and take advantage of a weakness that we are seeing of Canadian grades, heavier grades. And we're also addressing a wholesale opportunity in the area. El Dorado is a refinery that was built to run heavier than we running versus what we were running it, and we are trying to capture that opportunity.
Kalei Akamine
Research Analyst, Bank of America
I appreciate.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US
It's really kind of the limit when you think about El Dorado because of its configuration. In order to heavily benefit from optionality, make asphalt, improve our asphalt quality and net backs, and overall it will really contribute to that system capture.
Kalei Akamine
Research Analyst, Bank of America
I'm so sorry for interrupting, guys. My follow-up question is just trying to understand the scope of the work plan. It seems like it goes through 2025. I'm trying to understand if that suggests that 2025 CapEx is gonna be very similar to 2024, and I'll leave it there.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US
Are you asking about the 2025 scope for El Dorado?
Kalei Akamine
Research Analyst, Bank of America
Well, you lay out this capital commitment or these accomplishments for 2023 through 2025, I think on slide number seven. Given that the work plan-
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US
Yeah.
Kalei Akamine
Research Analyst, Bank of America
Is basically known for 2025. I'm trying to get a handle on what 2025 capital looks like if you've already defined the work. I'm trying to figure out if that's similar to 2024.
Joseph Israel
EVP of Operations, Delek US
Yeah. The entire scope for KSR is 2024 with the $115 million that we mentioned, and it's a part of our capital program for the year. With regards to El Dorado, there is no real cost estimate to this point. It's mostly commercial efforts and know-how and blending, and we will come back later in the future if we feel like you know, tanks or other upgrades will be needed. No, this is down the road, more than a year from now.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Yeah. The reason that, Kalei, the slide says 2024 to 2025, as you can see Big Spring, which is not related to capital, some of the upside is coming only in 2025. That's the reason the slide says 2024 to 2025. Don't read into that from a capital commitment to 2025, just to make it very clear. That was not the intent of the slide. The slide was saying that the benefit is gonna come over time, but the turnaround, which is the heavy capital during 2024, gonna be completed in 2024.
Kalei Akamine
Research Analyst, Bank of America
I got it. That's very clear. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from Jason Gabelman with TD Cowen. Please go ahead.
Jason Gabelman
Managing Director of Energy Equity Research, TD Cowen
Yeah. Hey, it's Jason Gabelman. Thanks for taking my questions. I wanted to ask about shareholder returns. It wasn't discussed yet. I think the past few press releases you had disclosed buybacks quarter to date at the time the press release came out for earnings. You didn't do that this quarter. Wondering if you have made any buybacks quarter to date and the outlook for repurchases through 2024.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Hey, thanks for the question. I will give an overview around what we are thinking and how we think about the capital return to investor. First of all, we are very committed to shareholder return. We had from a free cash flow this year over $146 million of return, $85 million of the buyback, and $61 million of dividend. We are committed to maintain the same philosophy going into 2024. You can probably appreciate that we bought 8%, of our shares in 2023. Nothing of what we are disclosing suggests any waiver of our approach. We are very committed to shareholder return. We want to see us as a market leader around it, and we are holding ourselves to that standard.
Jason Gabelman
Managing Director of Energy Equity Research, TD Cowen
Okay. Sorry, it's a bit difficult to hear you. Is that 8% level kind of something you feel like that's achievable either in 2024 and/or in a mid-cycle environment?
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Last year was not a mid-cycle environment. We want to do it from free cash flow. We are committed to that. It might be less, it might be more. It depends on market condition. I don't want to predict market condition. I'm optimistic about market condition, but you will hold me to that number, and I don't want to be held to a number that is market condition driven. You need to understand the state of mind is find ways to bring return to shareholder on the short term, midterm, and long term, and we are committed to all of them. You have seen us demonstrate that, Jason, last year very nicely. We did exactly what we said we're gonna do, and we're gonna keep doing what we say, we're gonna do.
Jason Gabelman
Managing Director of Energy Equity Research, TD Cowen
Okay, understood. Maybe just if you could comment on demand that you're seeing in the niche markets that you operate in.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
I think there was enough discussion about the weather in every one of our calls, so we're not gonna talk about the weather. Other than the weather, we have a very good niche market, and we are very blessed and optimistic around it.
Jason Gabelman
Managing Director of Energy Equity Research, TD Cowen
Okay, thanks.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
You bet.
Operator
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, should you have a question, please press star one. There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the conference over to Avigal. Please proceed.
Avigal Soreq
President and CEO, Delek US
Thank you. I would like to thank my colleagues around the table for a great quarter, to thank the board of director, our investor, obviously, that join us for this call, and most importantly, to our employees that make this company what it is. We talk again in the next quarter. Thank you, operator.
Operator
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, this concludes your conference call for today. We thank you for participating. As I say, please disconnect your lines.
